Our story

A single chair on Ngong Road, nine years ago

Maryann started out cutting hair for neighbours in a rented room off Ngong Road in 2017, with one clipper and a stool. Word spread through Kilimani faster than she could book appointments, and by 2019 she'd brought on two braiders and moved into a proper storefront.

Today Maryann's is a full salon and barbershop — barbers on one side, braiders on the other, and a shared bench in the middle where regulars sit with a cup of chai and wait their turn. We still train every junior stylist in-house, the same way Maryann was taught: hands-on, patiently, one head at a time.

What we stand for

Three things we don't compromise on

Craft

Technique over shortcuts

Every barber and braider trains for months before touching a paying client — fades are practiced on mannequins first, braid tension is checked by a senior stylist before you leave the chair.

Heritage

Styles rooted here

Cornrows, box braids, bald fades and beard sculpts that reflect what Nairobi actually wears — not styles copied from somewhere else and forced to fit.

Hospitality

Everyone gets a seat

Kids, first-timers, regulars who've been coming since 2017 — chai's on us while you wait, and no one gets rushed out of the chair.

Our people

Fourteen stylists, one standard

Six barbers, seven braiders and one colour specialist — most trained right here through our apprenticeship bench before earning their own chair.
